changes.change: Dedicated Document constructor/field reference explains stable source IDs, explicit upstream offsets, optional automatic positions, nonmutation of input objects, integer resolved outputs, and immutable replay conflicts.

Executable 2500-record source import example preserves existing upstream positions, fully consumes ingest_many, and retries an older 100-record batch. Separate executable example shows stable IDs without upstream offsets and automatic positions that remain unchanged on retry.
Prominent guidance says ingest_many is lazy and must be iterated; each yielded batch commits separately and earlier batches survive a later failure.
Executable preview example distinguishes intentional zero-emission filtering from document rejection. Explains no mutation, no reducer execution, and no guarantee that a later full batch fits.

Runnable persistent consumer drains all stable query pages and all change pages. CursorExpired replaces the entire local state from a new snapshot, rather than replaying additive totals onto the previous state.

Documented all externally visible cache statuses and the healthy missing-cache/replay combination. Explained cache bytes as disk metadata, the usable in-memory view, reused/checkpointed log offset, and status changes on checkpoint.
Linked the telemetry and catalogue onboarding examples and optional preview debugging without expanding the quickstart into a full consumer tutorial.

Compact standalone example uses a persistent temporary log, imports 2500 readings, compares five summary fields against a Python oracle, deduplicates an old source batch, consumes paged live changes, persists a consumer checkpoint, reopens, deletes the cache, replaces expired consumer state, and verifies every document and unchanged log SHA-256.
